messages.text:
Good rate — that's the cheap end. The B30 is $899, ~30 TH/s, pulls 360–450 W, so at 10¢ you're looking at roughly $29 a month in power running it 24/7. It's ~50 dB, quiet enough for an office or garage shelf.

What it buys you: a real draw at a full block (3.125 BTC) every ten minutes, forever, plus steady sats to your own wallet in between.

First miner, or adding to a setup?

At 9 cents the B30 runs about $26 a month in power, 24/7. That's the cheapest home-mining setup I can point at honestly — under 12¢ is where these make the most sense.

Where would it sit, and is this your first miner?

Then the B30 you're looking at is a good first machine — enclosed, ~50 dB, plugs in and runs, and it's the newest chip we sell. $899, ships Nov 30, 2026 (it's a batch pre-sale).

Honest alternative: the Magic Miner 40T is $799 for more hashrate, ships Nov 14, but it's a more open, hobbyist-style unit. The B30 is the easier first one.

Want me to set up the B30?

Straight answer: at home power rates the sats a 30 TH/s unit stacks usually come to less than the electricity, so there's no payback date I'd promise you.

What you're buying is the shot — every ten minutes it draws for a full block, 3.125 BTC, and it keeps drawing for years. Meanwhile it stacks real sats to your own wallet, no exchange, no KYC. And for a first miner it's the best way there is to actually learn how mining, pools and wallets work.

At $26 a month in power, that's the price of the ticket that never expires.
